query: For high-entropy-alloy bond coats used in thermal barrier coating systems for high-temperature applications, what single intervention could improve coating durability and reliability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a rare-earth-element doping in the high-entropy-alloy bond coat improves the durability and reliability of thermal barrier coating systems.
generation.material_initial_state: As-fabricated high-entropy-alloy bond coat without rare-earth-element doping
generation.intervention: Rare-earth-element doping of the high-entropy-alloy bond coat
generation.structural_mediator: Improved oxide scale adhesion and reduced thermal conductivity
generation.mechanism: Rare-earth elements promote the formation of a more adherent and slower-growing oxide scale, enhancing the thermal barrier coating's thermal cycling resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: 25% increase in coating lifespan compared to the untreated baseline
generation.baseline: Untreated high-entropy-alloy bond coat without rare-earth-element doping
generation.uncertainty: Lack of specific data on the optimal rare-earth-element doping concentration and its interaction with different high-entropy-alloy compositions

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative thermal cycling test of rare-earth-element doped and undoped high-entropy-alloy bond coats
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the rare-earth-element doped bond coat shows no significant improvement in coating lifespan or adverse effects on oxide scale adhesion, the hypothesis is falsified
